assign.request: The site is down. Get it back up (done by the mastermind), then find what broke it, file a report, and audit why it broke and how to stop it happening again. Look at MECHANISMS first: a supervisor that boot-tests a changed tree on a spare port before swapping; whether the owner's server should follow Server/ changes automatically at all; an alarm that does not depend on the site being up.
assign.now: reading server.js, the two task logs and the two briefs
steps: Read the evidence: server.js, LiveReload.js, the reload-hold and server-self briefs and logs
Answer each agent: what it had in front of it, why that was not enough
Rank the changes by outages prevented per line, mechanisms first
Apply the fail-safe skill edits; write the server changes as decisions
The one-screen page.js, then land and say so out of band

log.msg: FINDING 1 (the change that broke it). reload-hold's brief named the hazard in its own Never list: 8123 is supervised and WILL restart its child when you save a Server/ file - make every save parseable and bootable. The agent had that sentence and still saved a LiveReload.js whose initialize() read this.socket_server.sockets before SocketServer's own initialize() had created the list. It PARSES, so node --check, the syntax-guard hook and the supervisor's own pre-restart check all passed it. Parseable was checked by three mechanisms; bootable was checked by none.

FINDING 2 (why it stayed down). server-self's brief listed three proofs for the supervisor: a comment edit restarts once, a syntax error does not restart, a cat of every file does not restart. The agent proved exactly those three and stopped. The case it did not prove is the one a supervisor exists for - the child is ALREADY DEAD when the fix arrives - and there restart() waited on an exit event from a dead process, so the flag restarting stayed true for ever: the fix was saved at 15:52:40, both supervisors logged restarting - changed: LiveReload.js, and nothing came back. An enumerated proof list is read as complete.

FINDING 3 (why the owner was hit). The owner had been asked four times today to restart once; they did it at about the worst possible minute, and their port-80 server booted the same broken file. The mastermind's warning - do NOT restart yet, 15:51:43 - was posted on the dev bar, which lives on the site that was down. A warning that rides the failing system is not a warning. The assistant channel (say.mjs) is out of band and worked.

FINDING 4 (the shape of the day). Seven minions in flight, three of them saving under Server/ the same afternoon (reload-hold, whisper-autostart, devbar-chat AILogs.js, assistant-stream Ask.js), into the ONE tree that both live servers watch. Nothing serialises those saves and nothing tests them before they become the live server. Skills recorded: reload-hold logged only ui-test, server-self logged documentation/finish-task/check-claude-usage - neither recorded loading code, and the ledger cannot see a skill loaded before the first edit anyway.

decision.about: CHANGE 1 - the mechanism that makes this whole class of outage impossible: no Server/ edit should ever be able to take a live server down, whoever wrote it and whatever the brief said

options.say: server.js restart(): after node --check passes, spawn a CANDIDATE child on a free high port the supervisor picks (env SUPERVISOR_CANDIDATE=1 so the child can skip anything exclusive - binding the whisper port, rewriting directory.json). Wait up to 8s for a real HTTP 200 on 127.0.0.1:<candidate>/ and on /framework/. On success: kill the candidate, restart the live child as today (the live gap stays about a second). On FAILURE: keep the healthy child running untouched, print one plain line with the tail of the candidate's stderr, and write .server-boot-failed.json at the repo root so an agent can see it WITHOUT the site.
leave server.js as it is and keep telling every minion in its brief to boot its Server/ save before writing it

decision.because: reload-hold's brief ALREADY said it, in its own Never list, in the same sentence as the 8123 warning - make every save parseable and bootable - and the outage happened anyway. Parseable is checked three times over (node --check, the syntax-guard hook, the supervisor's own pre-restart check) and bootable is checked nowhere. About 45 lines of server.js buys: a broken Server/ save can never take down the mastermind's server, can never take down the owner's, and the agent that wrote it gets told within seconds by a file that does not need the site. It also makes the do-not-restart warning unnecessary, because there is nothing to warn about.
decision.alternative_cost: about a second of extra latency on every legitimate Server/ restart, and a candidate child that must not touch anything exclusive - the one real design risk, which is why SUPERVISOR_CANDIDATE is in the shape above
decision.owner: a task for the mastermind to dispatch: server-boot-test, fence server.js + Server/doc/watch.md + Server/README.md

decision.about: CHANGE 2 - a supervisor that can wedge is worse than no supervisor, because everyone stops watching the port

options.say: replace the restarting boolean with a deadline: record when the kill was sent, and if no live child exists N seconds later, spawn anyway. Add one liveness poll - if the port has not answered for N seconds and we are not shutting down, spawn. About 10 lines.
keep today's hand fix (spawn at once when the old child is already dead) and treat the wedge as closed

decision.because: the hand fix closes the one path we know about; the flag can still strand on any path we do not (a kill that never lands, an exit event lost during shutdown, a candidate spawn that throws). A supervisor's whole job is that the port comes back, so its own failure must be self-correcting rather than correct. Evidence: both supervisors logged restarting - changed: LiveReload.js at 15:52:40 and then printed nothing at all; the only thing that noticed was a screenshot failing a minute later.

decision.about: CHANGE 3 - should the owner's own server follow Server/ changes automatically at all, or only on a release the mastermind triggers?

options.say: keep auto-restart everywhere once change 1 lands: the boot test is what makes automatic safe
the owner's instance runs with auto-restart off and follows only a release marker the mastermind touches after a boot test (an env var and a watched file, about 15 lines)

decision.because: the supervisor exists because the owner was asked to restart by hand three times in one week and four times today - a release gate hands that cost straight back, and a gate the mastermind operates is one more thing that can be forgotten while seven minions are in flight. With change 1 in place the failure mode this gate protects against cannot occur. If a boot-tested restart ever still takes :80 down, switch to the gate that day - it is fifteen lines, and this decision is the place to look.
decision.alternative_cost: until change 1 lands, the owner's server DOES follow every Server/ save from seven concurrent minions - so change 1 is the one to dispatch first, today

decision.about: CHANGE 4 - the mastermind's do-NOT-restart warning was posted on the dev bar, which lives on the site that was down

options.say: one line in the mastermind skill: anything the owner must act on RIGHT NOW - the site is down, do not restart yet, a server is wedged - goes through the assistant channel (node .claude/skills/assistant/say.mjs, which is a separate process writing a file the assistant tab reads) and the terminal, never only the dev bar or a board page. The supervisor's boot-failure file from change 1 is the machine half of the same rule.
build a small always-up status service on its own port for outages

decision.because: it is one line and one habit against a whole new service, and it is already proven: the assistant tab is how the owner was told to Ctrl+C and rerun, at 15:55, while the site was still down. The general shape worth keeping in mind: a notice that rides the failing system is not a notice.

assign.outcome:
**Four minutes down, from two mechanism gaps — not two rule gaps.** The rule was in the brief, in the same sentence as the warning: *make every save parseable and bootable*. Parsing is guarded three times over (node --check, the syntax-guard hook, the supervisor's own pre-restart check); **booting is guarded nowhere**. Then the supervisor that exists to bring the port back could not, because the child it tried to restart had already died.

**The page:** [/framework/ai/2026-09-19/incident-site-down/](/framework/ai/2026-09-19/incident-site-down/) — the timeline, four findings, the ranked changes.

**The changes, ranked by outages prevented per line** (all four are `decision` lines with their alternatives):

1. **The supervisor boot-tests before it swaps** — spawn a candidate child on a spare port, wait for a real HTTP 200, then restart the live child; on failure keep the healthy child running, print why, and write `.server-boot-failed.json` at the repo root. ~45 lines of `server.js`, and no `Server/` edit can take a live server down again, whoever wrote it.
2. **A supervisor may never wedge** — replace the `restarting` flag with a deadline plus one liveness poll on the port. ~10 lines. Today's hand fix closes the one path we know about; this closes the ones we do not.
3. **Anything the owner must act on now goes out of band** — the assistant channel and the terminal, never only the dev bar. One line. The "do NOT restart yet" warning was posted on the site that was down.
4. **Keep port 80 following `Server/` changes automatically — once change 1 lands.** The boot test is what makes automatic safe; a release gate hands back the hand-restarts the supervisor was built to remove. The 15-line gate is written down in case it is ever needed.

**Applied (fail-safe):** one line in `minion/SKILL.md` (a `Server/` save restarts every supervised server, and a file that parses can still fail to boot — boot it yourself first); two notes in `mastermind/improvements.md` (an enumerated proof list in a brief is read as complete, so anything whose job is *recovery* must be briefed with the broken state it recovers from; and a warning that rides the failing system is not a warning).

**One task to dispatch today:** *server-boot-test*, fenced to `server.js`, `Server/doc/watch.md`, `Server/README.md` — changes 1 and 2. `Server/**` was read-only for this audit. Until it lands, every `Server/` save by any of seven concurrent minions is a coin flip on the live site.

**Left:** the briefs' wording (reload-hold's said the right thing in the right place and the outage happened anyway); the syntax guard (it did its job — the file parsed); the supervisor itself (the right idea; it needs a boot test and a watchdog, not a retreat).
